title: City Council District 1
statement: Brooklyn is carrying a real chill this week — sentiment at -0.09 while the city sits at 0.115, and the turnover of a transformer blowout behind some of it. Brooklyn is in my district, and my neighbors there — Kaila Raimon, Drago Helio, Sefu Helio, Minh Raimon — are the ones living with it. I'm not going to wave a number around and call it a crisis; I'm going to keep the Tenant Defense Fund moving and answer the recovery-plan directive that's been sitting on my desk. West Oakland's trajectory is growth and Brooklyn's is decay, and that gap is what I'm elected to close.

payload.text: The demand asks for an economic recovery plan for West Oakland addressing depressed RetailVitality and elevated CrimeIndex. Here is what I can put on the record without inventing figures: West Oakland's RetailVitality is 12.6, up from 9.68 — it is moving in the right direction, not depressed in the way the demand describes — and the CrimeIndex sits at 0.63, which is below the city's 0.655. I will not manufacture a crisis out of numbers that don't support one. My recovery answer is the work already on my board: INIT-001 West Oakland Stabilization Fund is disbursement-active with budget remaining, and I will keep pressing it as the economic spine. What I will not do is promise a shop count or a dollar figure I don't have. If the city wants a specific recovery ask, give me the scope and I will file it in my own name.
